near_miss.lead: *h1nómn̥ + *bher- 'bear a name': ON bar ... konongs nafn
near_miss.why_not: Only the ON pivot has the collocation; in the Irish, ainm and as-beir 'says' are in different clauses (name explanation, not bearing); in Thucydides προφέρει 'excels' does not govern ὄνομα; in the Armenian anown and berin belong to separate clauses. Filed as a search lead (Vedic, Greek tragedy).

search_lead.cognate: *h1nómn̥ 'name' + *bher- 'carry': ON bera nafn ~ Ved. nā́ma bhar- ~ Gk ὄνομα φέρω
search_lead.argument: ON bera konungs/tígnar nafn 'bear the title of king/rank' matches RV maghávā nā́ma bíbhrat (Indra 'bearing the name Maghavan', a title), and the fame-qualified Ved. śrútyam nā́ma bíbhrat matches Gk ὄνομα δυσκλεὲς φέρω (*ḱlew- in both qualifiers, with opposite value). Same verb-object relation in all three branches. Caveat: 'bear a name' is a natural metaphor (cf. English); the ON instances are late prose; the better-known inherited name formula is *h1nómn̥ dheh1- 'put a name'. Weak lead, not a claim.
